recipes.name: Plain Dosa
recipes.description: A crisp, golden crepe made from a fermented rice and urad dal batter, the everyday staple of any Tamil breakfast.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked idli rice and separately drain the urad dal with fenugreek seeds.
Grind the urad dal with fenugreek to a light, fluffy paste adding water little by little, then grind the rice to a slightly grainy paste.
Mix both pastes with salt in a large bowl to a pourable consistency and ferment covered in a warm place for 8 hours until bubbly.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium and sprinkle a few drops of water; it should sizzle and evaporate quickly.
Pour a ladle of batter at the centre and spread outward in a spiral into a thin round.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base turns golden and crisp, then fold and serve hot.

recipes.name: Masala Dosa
recipes.description: A crisp fermented dosa wrapped around a soft, turmeric-tinted potato masala tempered with onions and curry leaves.

ingredients.prep: soaked and ground into dosa batter
soaked and ground into dosa batter

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard seeds, add chana dal and fry till golden.
Add sliced onion, slit green chili and curry leaves; saute until the onion turns soft and translucent.
Stir in turmeric and salt, add the mashed potato with a splash of water and mix into a soft masala; keep warm.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin in a spiral.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base is golden and crisp.
Place a portion of potato masala along the centre, fold the dosa over it and serve hot with chutney.

recipes.name: Idli
recipes.description: Soft, pillowy steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal batter, the gentlest of Tamil breakfasts.

steps.instruction: Grind soaked urad dal with fenugreek to a fluffy paste, then grind the rice to a fine paste, adding water sparingly.
Combine both with salt into a thick batter and ferment covered in a warm spot for 8 hours until doubled and airy.
Grease the idli plates lightly with oil and pour a ladle of batter into each mould.
Add water to the steamer and bring to a rolling boil on high.
Place the stand inside, cover and steam on medium for 10 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Rest 2 minutes, then spoon out the idlis and serve hot with chutney and sambar.

recipes.name: Medu Vada
recipes.description: Crisp golden urad dal doughnuts, fluffy inside and studded with pepper and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked urad dal and grind to a thick, fluffy batter using minimal water.
Mix in crushed pepper, chopped green chili, ginger, curry leaves, asafoetida and salt; whip the batter till light.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium until a drop of batter rises steadily to the surface.
Wet your palm, take a lemon-sized ball, flatten it and poke a hole in the centre.
Slide the vada into the oil and fry, turning once, until golden and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper and serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

recipes.name: Ven Pongal
recipes.description: A comforting savoury porridge of rice and moong dal, richly seasoned with pepper, cumin, cashews and ghee.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the moong dal in the cooker on low until it smells nutty, then add rinsed rice.
Pour in about 3 cups of water with salt and pressure cook for 4 whistles until soft and mushy.
Heat ghee in a kadai, fry cashews until golden, then add cumin and crushed pepper.
Add chopped ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Mash the cooked rice-dal lightly, pour the tempering over it and mix well, loosening with hot water if needed.
Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, alongside sambar and coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Rava Upma
recipes.description: A fluffy, savoury semolina breakfast tempered with mustard, dals, ginger and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the rava in a kadai on low until it turns aromatic and slightly golden, then set aside.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal and cashews and fry until golden.
Add chopped onion, slit green chili, ginger and curry leaves; saute until the onion is soft.
Pour in about 1.5 cups of water with salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the flame and add the roasted rava in a slow stream while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook 2 minutes until the water is absorbed and fluffy; serve hot.

recipes.name: Rava Kesari
recipes.description: A glossy, ghee-laden semolina sweet flavoured with cardamom and studded with fried cashews and raisins.

ingredients.prep: or a pinch of food color

steps.instruction: Heat half the ghee in a kadai and fry cashews and raisins until golden and puffed; remove and set aside.
In the same ghee, roast the rava on low until fragrant without browning.
Bring about 1.25 cups of water with saffron to a boil in a separate pot.
Lower the flame and pour the hot water into the rava slowly while stirring to keep it lump-free.
Once the water is absorbed, add sugar and cardamom powder and stir until it melts and the mixture thickens.
Drizzle the remaining ghee, fold in the fried cashews and raisins, and serve warm.

recipes.name: Semiya Upma
recipes.description: A light vermicelli breakfast roasted till golden and tempered with mustard, dals and vegetables.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the vermicelli in a kadai on low until evenly golden, then set aside.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add onion, slit green chili, curry leaves, diced carrot and peas; saute until softened.
Pour in about 1.25 cups of water with salt and bring to a boil.
Add the roasted vermicelli, stir, cover and cook on low until the water is absorbed.
Fluff gently with a fork and serve hot.

recipes.name: Aval Upma
recipes.description: A quick, soft flattened-rice breakfast tempered with mustard, peanuts, onions and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Rinse the poha in a colander under water, drain fully and let it soften for 5 minutes.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal and peanuts and fry until golden.
Add chopped onion, green chili and curry leaves; saute until the onion softens.
Stir in turmeric and salt, then add the softened poha and gently mix to coat evenly.
Cover and cook 2 minutes until heated through and fluffy.
Squeeze over lemon juice, mix and serve hot.

recipes.name: Onion Uttapam
recipes.description: A thick, soft dosa-batter pancake topped with onions, tomato and green chili, griddled until golden.

ingredients.prep: soaked and ground into dosa batter
soaked and ground into dosa batter

steps.instruction: Mix the fermented batter with salt to a thick, spreadable consistency.
Combine chopped onion, tomato, green chili and coriander in a bowl to use as topping.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium and pour a ladle of batter, spreading into a thick round.
Scatter the onion-tomato topping over the surface and press lightly with the spatula.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook until the base is golden, then flip and cook the topping side briefly.
Serve hot with coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Adai
recipes.description: A hearty, protein-rich mixed-dal and rice pancake spiced with red chili, ginger and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked rice and dals and grind coarsely with red chili, ginger and asafoetida, keeping some texture.
Mix in salt, chopped curry leaves and onion to a thick batter; rest 20 minutes.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium and pour a ladle of batter, spreading into a thick round with a hole in the centre.
Drizzle oil around the edges and into the hole and cook until the base is crisp and golden.
Flip and cook the other side until crisp.
Serve hot with jaggery, avial or coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Semiya Idli
recipes.description: Soft, instant steamed cakes made from roasted vermicelli and rava with a light mustard-dal tempering.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a kadai, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, green chili and curry leaves and fry till golden.
Add the vermicelli and rava with grated carrot and roast on low until fragrant and lightly golden.
Cool slightly, then mix in a bowl with whisked curd, salt and enough water to a thick idli batter; rest 10 minutes.
Bring water in the steamer to a boil and grease the idli moulds.
Stir eno into the batter, pour into the moulds and steam on medium for 10 minutes.
Rest 2 minutes, unmould and serve hot with chutney.

recipes.name: Set Dosa
recipes.description: Thick, soft and spongy dosas served in a set, made from a slightly sour fermented batter.

steps.instruction: Grind soaked urad dal, fenugreek and poha to a fluffy paste, then grind the rice fine.
Mix with salt and sugar to a slightly thick batter and ferment 8 hours until airy.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium and pour a ladle of batter without spreading, keeping it thick and round.
Drizzle a little oil, cover and cook until the top is set with airy pores and the base is golden.
Flip briefly to cook the top side.
Stack in sets of three and serve hot with chutney and sagu.

recipes.name: Rava Dosa
recipes.description: A lacy, ultra-crisp instant dosa of semolina and rice flour speckled with cumin, pepper and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: In a bowl mix rava, rice flour, maida, cumin, crushed pepper, chopped chili, ginger, curry leaves, cashew and salt.
Whisk in about 1.5 cups of water to a very thin, watery batter with no lumps; rest 15 minutes.
Heat the dosa tawa on medium-high until very hot.
Stir the batter and pour it from a height across the tawa in a thin lacy layer, filling gaps.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook without disturbing until the base is deeply golden and crisp.
Fold and serve hot with coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Coconut Chutney
recipes.description: The classic white chutney of ground fresh coconut and roasted gram, finished with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering.

steps.instruction: Grind grated coconut, puffed gram, green chili, ginger and salt with a little water to a smooth chutney.
Transfer to a serving bowl and adjust consistency with water.
Heat oil in a small kadai, splutter mustard seeds, then add urad dal and broken red chili.
Add curry leaves and asafoetida and let them crackle for a few seconds.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the chutney and stir once before serving.

recipes.name: Tomato Chutney
recipes.description: A tangy, slightly spicy ground chutney of sauteed tomatoes, onion and red chili with a mustard tempering.

steps.instruction: Heat half the oil, fry urad dal and red chili until golden, then add garlic and onion and saute till soft.
Add chopped tomato and tamarind and cook until the tomato turns mushy and the oil separates.
Cool, add salt and grind to a coarse or smooth chutney as preferred.
Heat the remaining oil, splutter mustard seeds and add curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the chutney and serve with dosa or idli.

recipes.name: Tiffin Sambar
recipes.description: A mildly sweet, aromatic sambar of soft toor dal and shallots made specially to pair with idli and dosa.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric and a little water for 4 whistles until soft; mash and keep aside.
Heat oil in a pot, splutter mustard seeds, add red chili and curry leaves, then saute the peeled shallots until translucent.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft, then pour in the tamarind pulp with a cup of water.
Stir in sambar powder and salt and simmer until the raw smell disappears.
Add the mashed dal and coconut paste, adjust water and simmer to a smooth, slightly sweet sambar.
Serve hot with idli, dosa or pongal.

recipes.name: Idiyappam
recipes.description: Delicate steamed string hoppers pressed from soft rice-flour dough, light and lacy.

steps.instruction: Boil about 1 cup of water with salt and a few drops of coconut oil in a saucepan.
Pour the hot water gradually into the roasted rice flour, mixing to a soft, smooth, non-sticky dough.
Fill the dough into an idiyappam press and squeeze swirls of thin strands onto greased idli plates.
Scatter a little grated coconut over each and place in a steamer with boiling water.
Steam on medium for 8 minutes until the strands turn glossy and cooked through.
Serve warm with coconut milk, sweetened coconut or vegetable stew.

recipes.name: Kuzhi Paniyaram
recipes.description: Golden, crisp-shelled dumplings of dosa batter tempered with onion and cooked in a moulded pan.

steps.instruction: Heat a little oil, splutter mustard seeds, fry chana dal, then saute chopped onion, green chili, curry leaves and asafoetida until soft.
Fold this tempering and salt into the fermented dosa batter to a thick dropping consistency.
Heat the paniyaram pan on medium and add a few drops of oil into each mould.
Fill each mould three-quarters full with batter and cook until the base is golden and crisp.
Flip each paniyaram with a spoon and cook the other side until golden all over.
Serve hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

recipes.name: Sakkarai Pongal
recipes.description: A festive sweet pongal of rice and moong dal cooked with jaggery, ghee, cardamom, cashews and raisins.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the moong dal until nutty, add rinsed rice, milk and water, and pressure cook for 5 whistles until very soft.
Melt the grated jaggery with a splash of water into a syrup and strain out impurities.
Mash the cooked rice-dal, add the jaggery syrup and cook on low, stirring, until glossy and thick.
Heat ghee in a kadai and fry cashews and raisins until golden and puffed.
Stir the fried nuts, remaining ghee and cardamom powder into the pongal and mix well.
Serve warm as a sweet breakfast or festive offering.

recipes.name: Vatha Kuzhambu
recipes.description: A tangy, robust tamarind-based gravy tempered with sundried vathals and toasted spices, a Tamil household staple served with hot rice and ghee.

ingredients.prep: soaked in warm water and pulp extracted

steps.instruction: Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze and strain to extract a thick pulp; discard the fibres.
Peel the shallots and keep them whole. Measure out the sambar powder, turmeric and asafoetida into a small bowl.
Heat sesame oil in a kadai on medium flame. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add fenugreek seeds and broken red chillies and fry until the fenugreek turns golden.
Add curry leaves and whole shallots and saute until the shallots turn glossy and lightly browned at the edges.
Lower the flame, add sambar powder, turmeric and asafoetida and roast for 20 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the masala.
Pour in the tamarind extract along with another 100 ml water, add salt and jaggery, and stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered on medium-low until the kuzhambu thickens, turns glossy and oil floats on top, about 12 minutes. Serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Puli Kuzhambu
recipes.description: A hearty tamarind and vegetable gravy simmered with drumstick and brinjal, seasoned with ground coconut-coriander masala in the Tamil village style.

steps.instruction: Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm water and extract a thick pulp. Cut drumstick into batons and brinjal into wedges, keeping the brinjal in water to prevent browning.
Dry-roast coriander seeds lightly, then grind with grated coconut and a splash of water to a smooth paste in the mixer.
Heat sesame oil in a kadai on medium flame, splutter mustard seeds, add fenugreek seeds and curry leaves and fry until fragrant.
Add shallots and saute for two minutes, then add tomato and cook until softened and pulpy.
Add drumstick and brinjal along with sambar powder, turmeric and salt, and toss to coat in the masala.
Pour in tamarind extract and 150 ml water, cover and simmer until the vegetables turn tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the ground coconut paste and simmer a further 5 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns aromatic. Serve with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Vendakkai Poriyal
recipes.description: A dry okra stir-fry seasoned with mustard, urad dal and a final flourish of fresh grated coconut, a classic Tamil lunch side.

ingredients.prep: wiped dry and cut into thin rounds

steps.instruction: Wipe the okra completely dry with a cloth, trim the ends and slice into thin rounds; the dry surface keeps it from turning slimy.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium flame, splutter mustard seeds, then add urad dal, broken red chilli and curry leaves and fry until the dal turns golden.
Add the okra rounds and turmeric, and stir-fry uncovered on medium flame so the moisture escapes, about 5 minutes.
Add salt and red chilli powder, lower the flame and continue frying, stirring occasionally, until the okra is cooked through and no longer sticky, about 6 minutes.
Sprinkle grated coconut, toss for a minute and switch off. Serve as a side with rice and sambar.

recipes.name: Beans Poriyal
recipes.description: Finely chopped French beans steamed and stir-fried with a mustard-dal tempering and coconut, a simple everyday Tamil vegetable dish.

steps.instruction: String the beans and chop them as finely as possible into small even pieces so they cook quickly and evenly.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium flame, splutter mustard seeds, then add urad dal, chana dal, slit green chilli and curry leaves and fry until the dals turn golden.
Add the chopped beans and turmeric, toss well, then sprinkle 2 tablespoons water, cover and cook on low flame until just tender, about 7 minutes.
Add salt, uncover and stir-fry on medium for a minute to drive off excess moisture.
Add grated coconut, toss to combine and switch off. Serve warm alongside rice and rasam.

recipes.name: Cabbage Poriyal
recipes.description: Shredded cabbage lightly steamed and tempered with lentils, green chilli and coconut for a soft, mildly sweet Tamil stir-fry.

steps.instruction: Finely shred the cabbage, discarding the thick core, and rinse well in a colander.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium flame, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, chopped green chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida, and fry until the dal is golden.
Add the shredded cabbage and turmeric, toss well, cover and cook on low flame until wilted and tender, about 6 minutes, stirring once.
Add salt, uncover and stir-fry on medium for a minute; cabbage releases water so keep it dry.
Fold in the grated coconut, toss and switch off. Serve as a light side dish.

recipes.name: Kadalai Paruppu Kootu
recipes.description: A gentle chana dal and vegetable stew thickened with a ground coconut-cumin paste, mild and comforting in the Tamil kootu tradition.

steps.instruction: Rinse chana dal and pressure-cook it with turmeric and 200 ml water for 4 whistles until soft but not mushy.
While the dal cooks, peel and cube the bottle gourd, and grind grated coconut, cumin seeds and green chilli to a smooth paste with a little water.
In a kadai, boil the bottle gourd with a little salt in 150 ml water until tender, about 8 minutes.
Add the cooked chana dal and the ground coconut paste, mix and simmer for 5 minutes until the flavours meld and it thickens slightly.
In a small pan heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, broken red chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida, and fry until golden.
Pour the tempering over the kootu, stir and serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Milagu Rasam
recipes.description: A peppery, medicinal rasam brewed from freshly pounded black pepper, cumin and garlic in tamarind broth, soothing for colds and rainy days.

steps.instruction: Soak tamarind in 250 ml warm water and extract a thin juice. Coarsely pound black pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar to a coarse powder.
In a saucepan combine tamarind juice, chopped tomato, turmeric, asafoetida, curry leaves, salt and the pounded pepper-cumin mix along with 150 ml water.
Bring to a boil on medium flame, then lower to a gentle simmer; do not boil hard or the rasam turns bitter. Simmer until frothy on top, about 6 minutes.
Switch off the moment it begins to froth. In a small pan heat ghee, splutter mustard seeds and broken red chilli, and pour over the rasam.
Garnish with chopped coriander, cover for a minute to trap the aroma and serve hot with rice or as a warming drink.

recipes.name: Thakkali Rasam
recipes.description: A bright, tangy tomato rasam built on tamarind and rasam powder, mashed with garlic and finished with a ghee tempering and coriander.

steps.instruction: Soak tamarind in 250 ml warm water and extract juice. Chop tomatoes and crush the garlic.
In a saucepan mash the chopped tomatoes roughly with your hand or ladle, then add tamarind juice, rasam powder, turmeric, asafoetida, garlic, curry leaves, salt and 150 ml water.
Bring to a boil on medium flame, then reduce to low and simmer gently until frothy and aromatic, about 7 minutes; avoid a rolling boil.
In a small pan heat ghee, splutter mustard and cumin seeds with broken red chilli, and pour the tempering over the rasam.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice and a poriyal.

recipes.name: Thayir Sadam
recipes.description: Soft mashed rice mixed with fresh curd and milk, tempered with mustard, ginger and green chilli, the ultimate cooling Tamil comfort meal.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice slightly softer than usual and mash it lightly while still warm so it turns creamy.
Let the rice cool to lukewarm, then mix in the whisked curd, milk and salt to a soft, loose consistency; it thickens as it sits.
Heat oil in a small pan on medium, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, chopped green chilli, grated ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida and fry until the dal is golden.
Pour the hot tempering over the curd rice and fold it through.
Garnish with coriander and serve at room temperature, ideally with a spoon of pickle.

recipes.name: Puliyodarai
recipes.description: Rice coated in a spiced tamarind paste with roasted lentils, peanuts and sesame, the temple-style tangy tamarind rice of Tamil Nadu.

steps.instruction: Spread the cooked rice on a plate, drizzle a little sesame oil and let it cool so the grains separate.
Dry-roast fenugreek seeds and sesame seeds separately until fragrant, then grind to a fine powder.
Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm water and extract a thick pulp.
Heat sesame oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard seeds, then add chana dal, peanuts, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry until the dal and peanuts turn golden.
Add turmeric and asafoetida, then pour in the tamarind pulp with salt and simmer until the paste thickens, darkens and the oil separates, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the roasted fenugreek-sesame powder and cook for one more minute; this pulikachal can be stored and used as needed.
In a bowl, gently mix the cooled rice with enough tamarind paste to coat, adjust salt and rest 10 minutes for the flavours to soak in. Serve with papad.

recipes.name: Thakkali Sadam
recipes.description: Fragrant rice cooked with a spiced onion-tomato masala and whole garam spices, a quick and flavourful Tamil one-pot lunch.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice with a little extra water so grains stay separate, spread out and cool.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard seeds, add cinnamon, cloves and curry leaves, then add sliced onion and saute until soft and golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and fry until the raw smell goes, then add chopped tomatoes with turmeric, red chilli powder and salt.
Cook the masala on low, mashing the tomatoes, until it turns thick, pulpy and oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Add the cooled rice and gently fold it into the masala until every grain is coated and evenly coloured.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with raita or chips.

recipes.name: Thengai Sadam
recipes.description: Cooled rice tossed with freshly grated coconut and a crunchy tempering of lentils, cashews and green chilli, mild and aromatic.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice so grains stay separate, spread out and cool completely, then add salt and fluff.
Heat coconut oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard seeds, then add urad dal, chana dal and cashews and fry until golden.
Add slit green chilli, broken red chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida and fry for 20 seconds.
Lower the flame, add the grated coconut and roast gently just until it loses its raw smell and turns fragrant, without browning, about 3 minutes.
Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together until evenly mixed. Switch off and serve warm.

recipes.name: Tamil Vegetable Biryani
recipes.description: Basmati rice layered with a mint-coriander vegetable masala and whole spices, a fragrant South Indian style veg biryani.

steps.instruction: Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain. Dice all the vegetables while it soaks.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker on medium, add cinnamon, then the sliced onion and fry until golden.
Add ginger garlic paste, mint and coriander, saute a minute, then add tomato and cook until soft.
Add the vegetables, biryani masala, whisked curd and salt, and saute for 3 minutes until well coated.
Add the drained rice and 120 ml water, stir gently and bring to a boil.
Close the lid and cook on low for 1 whistle, then switch off and let the pressure release naturally.
Open, fluff gently with a fork to keep grains intact and serve hot with raita.

recipes.name: Mor Kuzhambu
recipes.description: A soothing buttermilk curry thickened with a ground coconut-lentil-cumin paste, gently spiced and never boiled hard to keep it silky.

steps.instruction: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes. Whisk the curd with 150 ml water into a smooth buttermilk and keep aside.
Grind grated coconut, soaked chana dal, cumin and green chilli to a smooth paste with a little water.
In a kadai boil the ash gourd cubes with turmeric and salt in 150 ml water until tender, about 8 minutes.
Add the ground paste, mix and simmer 3 minutes until it loses the raw taste and thickens.
Lower the flame fully, stir in the buttermilk and warm through only until steaming; do not let it boil or it will curdle. Switch off.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan, splutter mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, broken red chilli and curry leaves, and pour over the kuzhambu. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Ennai Kathirikai
recipes.description: Small brinjals stuffed and simmered in a roasted peanut-sesame-coconut masala with tamarind, a rich Chettinad-style gravy.

ingredients.prep: small, slit into quarters keeping stem intact

steps.instruction: Slit each small brinjal into quarters from the base keeping the stem end intact, and drop into water to prevent browning.
Dry-roast peanuts, sesame seeds, dry coconut, coriander seeds and red chillies until golden and fragrant, then grind to a coarse-thick masala.
Stuff a little of the ground masala into the slit brinjals, reserving the rest.
Heat sesame oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves, then place the stuffed brinjals and saute gently, turning, until skins blister, about 5 minutes.
Add the remaining masala, turmeric, tamarind pulp, salt and 150 ml water, stir carefully around the brinjals.
Cover and simmer on low until the brinjals are soft and the gravy turns thick and oil floats on top, about 15 minutes. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Avial
recipes.description: A medley of mixed vegetables cooked and bound in a coconut-cumin-curd paste finished with raw coconut oil and curry leaves, a festive Tamil favourite.

steps.instruction: Cut all the vegetables into uniform finger-length batons so they cook evenly.
Coarsely grind grated coconut, cumin and green chilli without water to a thick, chunky paste.
In a kadai cook the harder vegetables first, drumstick and carrot, in 150 ml water with turmeric and salt for 5 minutes, then add the rest and cook until just tender.
Add the coconut paste and mix gently without mashing the vegetables, simmering for 3 minutes.
Lower the flame, stir in the whisked curd and warm through without boiling.
Switch off, drizzle raw coconut oil, scatter torn curry leaves and cover for 2 minutes. Serve with rice or adai.

recipes.name: Paruppu (Tamil Dal)
recipes.description: Soft toor dal mashed with ghee, green chilli and a mustard-cumin tempering, the plain comforting dal eaten with rice and ghee across Tamil homes.

steps.instruction: Rinse the toor dal and pressure-cook with the chopped tomato, slit green chilli, turmeric and 200 ml water for 4 whistles until very soft.
Open the cooker, add salt and mash the dal well with a ladle to a smooth consistency, adding a little hot water if too thick.
Heat ghee in a small pan on medium, splutter mustard and cumin seeds, then add broken red chilli, crushed garlic, curry leaves and asafoetida and fry until golden.
Pour the tempering over the dal, stir and simmer for a minute.
Serve hot over steamed rice with a little extra ghee.

recipes.name: Chicken Chettinad
recipes.description: Chicken simmered in a bold freshly-roasted Chettinad masala of peppercorns, fennel, stone flower and coconut, fiery and deeply aromatic.

steps.instruction: Dry-roast black pepper, fennel, coriander seeds, red chillies and stone flower on low until fragrant, then grind with grated coconut and a little water to a fine masala paste.
Heat oil in a kadai on medium, add curry leaves and chopped onion and fry until deep golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and fry until the raw smell goes, then add tomato and turmeric and cook until pulpy.
Add the chicken pieces and salt and saute on high for 4 minutes to sear and seal the meat.
Add the ground Chettinad masala, stir to coat, then add 150 ml water, cover and simmer on low until the chicken is tender, about 18 minutes.
Uncover and cook on medium a few minutes to thicken the gravy and let the oil separate. Serve with rice or dosa.

recipes.name: Meen Kuzhambu
recipes.description: A tangy, spicy fish curry simmered in tamarind gravy with shallots and a roasted spice-coconut base, best eaten a day later with rice.

steps.instruction: Clean the fish steaks and rub with a little turmeric and salt. Soak tamarind and extract a thick pulp.
Grind grated coconut and coriander seeds with a little water to a smooth paste.
Heat sesame oil in a kadai on medium, splutter mustard and fenugreek seeds and curry leaves, then add shallots and fry until soft.
Add tomato, turmeric and red chilli powder and cook until the tomato breaks down, then add the coconut paste and fry a minute.
Pour in the tamarind pulp and 150 ml water with salt, bring to a boil and simmer 8 minutes to cook out the raw tamarind.
Slide in the fish pieces, do not stir vigorously, and simmer on low until the fish is cooked and the gravy thickens, about 10 minutes.
Switch off and rest at least 30 minutes before serving with hot rice; the flavour deepens over time.

recipes.name: Mutton Kuzhambu
recipes.description: Tender mutton pressure-cooked and simmered in a fragrant onion-tomato and roasted coconut masala, a rich Tamil non-veg gravy.

steps.instruction: Dry-roast fennel, pepper and grated coconut on low until golden, then grind to a smooth paste with a little water.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker on medium, add cinnamon and curry leaves, then the chopped onion and fry until deep golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and fry off the raw smell, then add tomato with turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder and cook until pulpy.
Add the mutton and salt and saute on high for 5 minutes to sear the meat well.
Add the ground coconut paste and 250 ml water, close the lid and pressure-cook for about 6 whistles until the mutton is tender.
Release pressure, open and simmer uncovered on medium until the gravy thickens to a glossy consistency. Serve with rice or idli.

recipes.name: Murukku
recipes.description: Crunchy spiral-shaped savoury snack pressed from a rice and urad dal flour dough and deep-fried, a Tamil Diwali staple.

steps.instruction: In a mixing bowl combine rice flour, finely ground roasted urad dal flour, cumin seeds, sesame seeds, asafoetida, softened butter and salt.
Add water little by little and knead into a smooth, non-sticky pliable dough.
Heat oil in a kadai until a small piece of dough sizzles and rises steadily.
Fill the dough into a murukku press with the star plate and squeeze concentric spirals directly onto a greased ladle or flat surface.
Slide the spirals into the hot oil and fry, turning once, until the sizzling subsides and they turn golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely before storing airtight.

recipes.name: Thattai
recipes.description: Flat, crisp, round savoury crackers made from rice flour studded with chana dal and sesame, deep-fried till golden.

steps.instruction: In a bowl mix rice flour, ground urad dal, soaked chana dal, sesame seeds, red chili powder, chopped curry leaves, asafoetida, salt and a teaspoon of hot oil.
Add water gradually and knead to a smooth stiff dough; rest it for ten minutes.
Pinch small balls and flatten each thinly into a round disc on a greased sheet, pricking with a fork to prevent puffing.
Heat oil in a kadai to medium hot.
Fry the discs a few at a time, flipping once, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and cool before storing airtight.

recipes.name: Mysore Pak
recipes.description: Rich melt-in-the-mouth sweet of besan cooked with copious ghee and sugar syrup, cut into fudge-like squares.

steps.instruction: Grease a small tray and keep the warm ghee-oil mixture ready beside the stove.
In a kadai dissolve sugar in a little water and boil to a one-string consistency syrup.
Lower the flame and whisk in the sifted besan steadily, breaking all lumps.
Add the warm ghee-oil a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly as the mixture absorbs the fat and turns frothy and porous.
When the mixture leaves the sides and looks aerated, pour immediately into the greased tray.
Cut into squares while still warm and cool completely before removing.

recipes.name: Coconut Burfi
recipes.description: Soft fudge of fresh grated coconut cooked with sugar and ghee, fragrant with cardamom and set into diamonds.

steps.instruction: Grease a plate or tray and keep ready.
In a kadai combine grated coconut, sugar and milk and cook on medium flame, stirring, until the sugar melts.
Continue stirring as the mixture thickens and the moisture evaporates.
Add ghee, cardamom powder and chopped cashews and stir until the mass leaves the sides of the pan.
Pour into the greased tray and spread evenly.
Cut into diamonds while warm and cool completely before separating.

recipes.name: Rava Ladoo
recipes.description: Roasted semolina ladoos bound with ghee and sugar, dotted with fried cashews and raisins and scented with cardamom.

steps.instruction: Fry cashews and raisins in a little ghee until golden and the raisins plump, then set aside.
In the same kadai dry roast the rava on low flame until fragrant but not browned.
Cool slightly and grind the rava to a coarse powder if a smoother ladoo is preferred.
Mix the roasted rava with powdered sugar, cardamom powder and the fried nuts and raisins.
Drizzle warm melted ghee and a splash of warm milk and mix until the mixture holds together.
Press firmly into round ladoos while warm and let them set.

recipes.name: Boondi Ladoo
recipes.description: Festive ladoos of tiny fried besan pearls soaked in cardamom sugar syrup and pressed into balls.

steps.instruction: Whisk besan with water and a pinch of food color into a smooth flowing batter of pouring consistency.
Boil sugar with a little water and cardamom powder to a sticky one-string syrup and keep warm.
Heat oil in a kadai; hold a perforated ladle over it and pour batter through so droplets fall as tiny boondi.
Fry the boondi till just cooked but not crisp, drain and drop straight into the warm syrup.
Add fried cashews and ghee and let the boondi soak until the syrup is absorbed.
While still warm, press handfuls firmly into round ladoos and let them set.

recipes.name: Semiya Payasam
recipes.description: Creamy vermicelli kheer simmered in milk with sugar, ghee-fried cashews and raisins and cardamom.

steps.instruction: Fry cashews and raisins in ghee until golden, remove and set aside.
In the same ghee roast the vermicelli until light golden.
Pour in the milk and simmer, stirring, until the vermicelli is soft.
Add sugar and cardamom powder and cook until slightly thickened.
Stir in the fried cashews and raisins and switch off.
Serve warm or chilled, adding a little hot milk if it thickens on standing.

recipes.name: Paruppu Payasam
recipes.description: Traditional moong dal payasam sweetened with jaggery and enriched with coconut milk, ghee-fried cashews and dry ginger.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the moong dal until aromatic and golden, then rinse.
Pressure cook the dal with water until soft and mashable.
Melt the jaggery with a little water into a syrup and strain into the cooked dal.
Simmer the dal and jaggery together until well blended, then lower the flame.
Stir in the coconut milk, cardamom powder and dry ginger and warm through without boiling.
Top with cashews fried golden in ghee and serve warm.

recipes.name: Urulaikizhangu Bonda
recipes.description: Spiced mashed potato balls dipped in seasoned besan batter and deep-fried to a crisp golden shell, a classic tea-time snack.

steps.instruction: Temper mustard seeds in a little oil, add onion, green chili, ginger, curry leaves, turmeric and asafoetida and saute until the onion softens.
Mix in the mashed potato and salt, cook briefly and cool the filling.
Roll the potato mixture into lime-sized balls.
Whisk besan, rice flour, a pinch of salt and water into a smooth coating batter.
Heat oil in a kadai, dip each ball in the batter and slide into the hot oil.
Fry, turning, until golden and crisp, drain and serve hot with chutney.

recipes.name: Vengaya Bajji
recipes.description: Sliced onions coated in a spiced besan batter and deep-fried into crisp fritters, a monsoon and tea-shop favourite.

steps.instruction: In a bowl whisk besan, rice flour, red chili powder, asafoetida, curry leaves, a pinch of baking soda and salt.
Add water gradually to form a thick, smooth coating batter.
Heat oil in a kadai to medium hot.
Dip each onion ring into the batter to coat well.
Slide the coated rings into the hot oil and fry, turning, until golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with coconut chutney or ketchup.

recipes.name: Konda Kadalai Sundal
recipes.description: Boiled chickpeas tempered with mustard, red chili and curry leaves and tossed with fresh grated coconut, a Navaratri offering.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with salt and water until soft but firm, then drain.
Heat coconut oil in a kadai and splutter mustard seeds, then add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add broken red chili, green chili, curry leaves and asafoetida and saute a few seconds.
Tip in the drained chickpeas and toss to coat with the tempering.
Add grated coconut, adjust salt and toss on low flame for a minute.
Serve warm as a festive snack.

recipes.name: Ribbon Pakoda
recipes.description: Flat crunchy ribbons of rice and besan flour spiced with chili and asafoetida, pressed and deep-fried for Diwali.

steps.instruction: Combine rice flour, besan, red chili powder, sesame seeds, asafoetida, softened butter and salt in a bowl.
Add water gradually and knead into a smooth pliable dough.
Heat oil in a kadai to medium hot.
Fit the flat ribbon plate into a press, fill with dough and squeeze ribbons directly into the hot oil in a circular motion.
Fry, flipping once, until the sizzling stops and the ribbons are golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely before storing airtight.

recipes.name: Filter Coffee
recipes.description: South Indian degree coffee brewed as a strong decoction in a metal filter, mixed with hot frothy milk and sugar.

steps.instruction: Add the coffee powder to the upper chamber of a South Indian metal coffee filter and press gently with the disc.
Pour just-boiled water over the powder, cover and let the strong decoction drip through into the lower chamber.
Boil the milk in a saucepan until hot and frothy.
In a tumbler add sugar and the desired amount of decoction, then pour in the hot milk.
Froth by pouring back and forth between the tumbler and davara until foamy.
Serve piping hot.

recipes.name: Rose Milk
recipes.description: Chilled sweet milk flavoured and coloured with fragrant rose, a refreshing summer drink from Tamil bakeries.

steps.instruction: Warm a little milk and dissolve the sugar in it, then cool.
Combine the sweetened milk with the remaining chilled milk.
Stir in the rose water and a pinch of rose pink food color.
Whisk well until frothy and evenly coloured.
Pour into a chilled tumbler over ice and serve cold.

recipes.name: Dalma
recipes.description: Odisha's iconic temple-style lentil and vegetable stew where toor dal is simmered with vegetables and finished with a roasted cumin-chilli tempering, cooked without onion or garlic.

steps.instruction: Rinse the toor dal well and add it to the pressure cooker with grated ginger, turmeric, salt and about 1.5 cups of water.
Add the cubed pumpkin, raw banana, brinjal and potato to the cooker, then pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until the dal is soft but the vegetables still hold shape.
While the dal cooks, dry-roast the cumin seeds and one dried red chilli in a frying pan until fragrant, then coarsely crush them in a mortar or by hand.
Once pressure releases, open the cooker, stir in the roasted cumin-chilli powder and grated coconut, and simmer for 3-4 minutes to a thick pourable consistency.
Heat the ghee in the frying pan, drop in a pinch of cumin, let it splutter, then pour this tempering over the dalma and cover for a minute before serving with rice.

recipes.name: Mixed Vegetable Santula
recipes.description: A light, lightly spiced Odia medley of boiled seasonal vegetables mashed loosely and finished with a garlic-panch-phoron tempering in mustard oil.

steps.instruction: Boil the potato, brinjal, pumpkin, papaya and tomato with turmeric, salt and just enough water in a deep pot until fork-tender, about 12 minutes.
Lightly mash the boiled vegetables with the back of a ladle so they stay chunky, not pureed, and keep the cooking liquid.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai until it just smokes, then add panch phoron, crushed garlic and slit green chilli and fry until the garlic turns golden.
Tip the mashed vegetables into the tempering, stir well, and simmer for 4-5 minutes until thick and glossy, adjusting salt before serving.

recipes.name: Aloo Besara
recipes.description: Comforting Odia potato curry in a pungent ground-mustard and garlic gravy tempered with panch phoron in mustard oil.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked mustard seeds with garlic and green chilli and a splash of water into a smooth, slightly runny paste; strain if you want it less bitter.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai to smoking, lower the flame and temper panch phoron and the dried red chilli until aromatic.
Add the potato wedges with turmeric and salt, and saute for 3-4 minutes so the edges lightly brown.
Pour in the mustard-garlic paste with about a cup of water, cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender and the gravy thickens, 10-12 minutes.
Finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil and chopped coriander, and serve with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Besara (Mixed Vegetable Mustard Curry)
recipes.description: A classic Odia besara of pumpkin, brinjal and raw banana simmered in a fiery ground mustard-and-cumin paste with garlic.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked mustard seeds, cumin seeds, garlic and one red chilli with a little water to a smooth paste.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai until smoking, add the remaining dried red chilli, then add all the vegetables with turmeric and salt.
Saute the vegetables for 4-5 minutes until they take on light colour at the edges.
Stir in the mustard paste with about a cup of water, cover and simmer 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the gravy clings to them.
Drizzle a teaspoon of raw mustard oil over the top and rest covered for two minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Ghanta Tarkari
recipes.description: A festive Odia mixed-vegetable and lentil curry with black chana and a fragrant roasted-coconut and cumin masala, traditionally made for Nuakhai and pujas.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked black chana with salt and water for 4-5 whistles until just tender, and set aside with the stock.
While the chana cooks, dry-roast the grated coconut, cumin seeds and red chillies in a kadai until deep golden and grind to a coarse paste with a little water.
Heat oil in the kadai, temper panch phoron, then add the potato, pumpkin, raw banana and yam with turmeric and salt and saute 5 minutes.
Add the cooked chana with its stock, cover and simmer until all vegetables are soft, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the roasted coconut-cumin paste and cook another 4-5 minutes until the gravy is thick and aromatic.
Finish with a spoon of ghee, cover for a minute and serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Saga Bhaja
recipes.description: Everyday Odia stir-fried leafy greens sauteed with garlic, dried red chilli and panch phoron in mustard oil until just wilted.

steps.instruction: Heat mustard oil in a kadai until it just smokes, then temper panch phoron and the broken dried red chillies.
Add the sliced garlic and onion and fry until the garlic is golden and fragrant.
Tip in the chopped greens with turmeric and salt, tossing on high heat so they wilt quickly.
Stir-fry uncovered until any released water evaporates and the greens are glossy and dry, about 4 minutes, then serve.

recipes.name: Badi Chura
recipes.description: A rustic Odia mash of crushed fried lentil badi with raw onion, garlic, green chilli and a drizzle of pungent mustard oil, eaten with hot rice and dal.

steps.instruction: Heat 1 teaspoon mustard oil in a frying pan and shallow-fry the badi on low heat until deep golden and crisp, then drain.
Let the fried badi cool a minute, then pound it coarsely in a mortar and pestle so it stays crumbly, not powdered.
In a bowl combine the crushed badi with chopped onion, garlic, green chilli, coriander and salt.
Drizzle over the remaining raw mustard oil and mix with your fingers until everything is well coated, then serve alongside rice.

recipes.name: Aloo Bharta
recipes.description: Odia-style mashed potato seasoned with raw onion, garlic, green chilli and generous mustard oil, a homely staple with dal-rice.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the potatoes for 3-4 whistles, then cool, peel and mash them coarsely in a mixing bowl.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, green chilli, coriander and salt to the mashed potato.
Pour in the raw mustard oil and mix thoroughly by hand, mashing so the aromatics are evenly distributed.
Shape into small rounds if you like and serve with steaming rice and a spoon of dal.

recipes.name: Baigana Bharta (Odia Style)
recipes.description: Smoky roasted brinjal mashed with mustard oil, raw onion, garlic and green chilli in the simple Odia home style.

steps.instruction: Rub the brinjals with a little mustard oil and roast them directly over an open flame or on a tawa, turning, until the skin is charred and the flesh collapses.
Cool the roasted brinjals, peel away the charred skin and mash the smoky flesh in a mixing bowl.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, green chilli, tomato, coriander and salt to the mashed brinjal.
Drizzle over the raw mustard oil and mix well, then serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Dahi Baigana
recipes.description: Fried brinjal slices bathed in a lightly spiced whisked yogurt sauce with a mustard-seed and curry-leaf tempering, a cooling Odia favourite.

steps.instruction: Rub the brinjal rounds with turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry them in mustard oil until golden and soft on both sides; drain and set aside.
Whisk the curd smooth in a bowl with a little salt and a pinch of turmeric, then gently arrange or fold in the fried brinjal.
In the leftover oil temper mustard seeds, cumin, dried red chilli, curry leaves and slit green chilli until they crackle.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the yogurt-brinjal, mix lightly and serve at room temperature with rice.

recipes.name: Sajana Chhuin Rai
recipes.description: Tender drumstick segments simmered in a sharp ground-mustard gravy with potato, a springtime Odia classic.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked mustard seeds with garlic and green chilli to a smooth paste with a little water.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai until smoking, temper cumin seeds and the dried red chilli.
Add the drumstick pieces and potato with turmeric and salt and saute for 4-5 minutes.
Pour in the mustard paste with about a cup of water, cover and simmer until the drumstick flesh is soft and pulpy, about 12 minutes.
Check the seasoning, drizzle raw mustard oil on top and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Kakharu Bhaja
recipes.description: Sweetish pumpkin slices pan-fried in mustard oil with panch phoron until caramelised at the edges, a quick Odia side.

steps.instruction: Toss the pumpkin slices with turmeric, red chilli powder and salt and let them sit for five minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a frying pan until smoking, then temper panch phoron and the dried red chilli.
Lay the pumpkin slices in a single layer and fry undisturbed for 3-4 minutes so the underside caramelises.
Flip and continue cooking until both sides are golden and the pumpkin is fork-tender, then serve hot.

recipes.name: Muga Dali (Roasted Moong Dal)
recipes.description: A fragrant Odia moong dal where the lentils are dry-roasted before cooking and finished with a ghee, cumin and dried-chilli tempering.

steps.instruction: Dry-roast the moong dal in a frying pan on low heat, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns light golden.
Transfer the roasted dal to the pressure cooker with chopped tomato, grated ginger, turmeric, salt and 1.5 cups water, and cook for 3-4 whistles.
Open the cooker, whisk the dal smooth and simmer to a comfortable pouring consistency, adding hot water if needed.
Heat ghee in the frying pan and temper cumin seeds, dried red chilli and slit green chilli until they splutter.
Pour the tempering over the dal, garnish with coriander and serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Kanika
recipes.description: Odisha's fragrant sweet pulao of ghee-fried rice cooked with cashews, raisins, jaggery and whole spices, offered at temples and served at feasts.

steps.instruction: Heat ghee in a deep pot and fry the cashews to light gold, then the raisins until they plump; scoop both out and reserve.
In the same ghee add bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them release their aroma.
Add the drained rice with a pinch of turmeric and salt and gently toast for 2-3 minutes until the grains are coated and glossy.
Pour in about 1.25 cups hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is almost done and the water absorbed.
Sprinkle over the grated jaggery and sugar, fold gently, cover and steam another 3-4 minutes until melted and glazed.
Fluff with a fork, scatter the fried cashews and raisins on top and serve warm.

recipes.name: Tomato Khata
recipes.description: A sweet-and-sour Odia tomato chutney-curry cooked with jaggery, dates and a panch-phoron tempering, served as a tangy end to a rice meal.

steps.instruction: Heat mustard oil in a kadai until smoking, then temper panch phoron and the dried red chilli until they crackle.
Add the chopped tomatoes with turmeric and salt and cook until they break down into a soft pulp, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the grated jaggery, chopped dates and raisins with a splash of water and simmer until glossy and jammy.
Adjust the sweet-sour balance to taste and cool slightly before serving as an accompaniment to rice.

recipes.name: Saga Dalma
recipes.description: A green variation of Odisha's beloved dalma where toor dal is cooked with leafy greens, colocasia and a roasted-spice finish, all without onion or garlic.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the toor dal with colocasia, pumpkin, grated ginger, turmeric, salt and 1.5 cups water for 3-4 whistles.
While the dal cooks, dry-roast cumin seeds and one red chilli in a frying pan and crush them coarsely.
Open the cooker, add the chopped spinach and grated coconut and simmer 4-5 minutes until the greens wilt into the dal.
Stir in the roasted cumin-chilli powder and adjust to a thick, stew-like consistency.
Heat ghee in the frying pan, splutter the remaining red chilli, pour over the dalma and cover for a minute before serving.

recipes.name: Macha Besara
recipes.description: Fried fish steaks simmered in a pungent ground-mustard gravy with garlic and tomato, one of Odisha's signature fish dishes.

steps.instruction: Rub the fish steaks with half the turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until golden on both sides and remove.
Grind the soaked mustard seeds, cumin and garlic to a smooth paste with a little water; strain if desired.
In the same kadai temper the dried red chilli, add chopped tomato with remaining turmeric and salt and cook until pulpy.
Add the mustard paste and slit green chillies with a cup of water and simmer 5 minutes to cook off the raw pungency.
Slide the fried fish into the gravy, simmer gently for 4-5 minutes, finish with raw mustard oil and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Macha Jhola
recipes.description: The everyday Odia fish curry of fried fish in a light onion, garlic and tomato gravy scented with cumin and turmeric.

steps.instruction: Marinate the fish with half the turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until crisp-edged and set aside.
In the same oil fry the potato wedges until lightly golden and remove.
Temper cumin seeds, add chopped onion and crushed garlic and fry until the onion is soft and golden.
Add tomato, remaining turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin powder and salt and cook to a thick masala, then add the potatoes and about a cup of water.
Simmer until the potato is nearly done, slide in the fried fish and cook gently 5 minutes, garnish with coriander and serve.

recipes.name: Chingudi Jhola
recipes.description: Odia prawn curry with prawns sauteed in mustard oil and simmered in a spiced onion-tomato-garlic gravy.

steps.instruction: Toss the prawns with a little turmeric and salt, flash-fry in hot mustard oil for a minute until they curl and turn pink, then remove.
In the same oil fry the potato cubes until golden at the edges and set aside.
Temper cumin seeds, add chopped onion and fry until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook off the raw smell.
Add tomato, remaining turmeric, red chilli powder and salt and cook to a thick masala, then add potatoes with a cup of water and simmer until nearly done.
Return the prawns, sprinkle garam masala and simmer just 3-4 minutes so they stay tender, garnish with coriander and serve.

recipes.name: Odia Chicken Curry (Kukuda Mansa)
recipes.description: A home-style Odisha chicken curry cooked in mustard oil with a robust onion-ginger-garlic base, potatoes and freshly warming spices.

steps.instruction: Marinate the chicken with whisked curd, half the turmeric, red chilli powder and salt for at least 15 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in the pressure cooker to smoking, temper bay leaf and cinnamon, then fry the potato halves until golden and remove.
Add chopped onion and fry until deep golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw aroma disappears.
Add tomato with the remaining turmeric and chilli powder and cook to a thick masala that releases oil.
Add the marinated chicken and fry on high heat for 5 minutes to seal, stirring so the masala coats every piece.
Return the potatoes, add about a cup of hot water, close the cooker and cook for 2-3 whistles until the chicken is tender.
Release pressure, stir in garam masala, simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes to thicken the gravy and serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Pakhala Bhata
recipes.description: Odisha's beloved summer staple of cooked rice fermented overnight in water, served cool with a tempering and green chili.

steps.instruction: Cook the washed raw rice in plenty of water until soft, then drain and let it cool to room temperature.
Transfer cooled rice to an earthen or steel pot, cover with water and a spoon of curd, and leave to ferment overnight or at least 6 hours.
Next day, stir the fermented rice with its water, add salt and a squeeze of lemon, and mash lightly with your hand.
Heat oil in a small pan, crackle mustard seeds, add slit green chilies and curry leaves, and pour this tempering over the pakhala.
Serve cool with fried or mashed vegetables on the side.

recipes.name: Dahi Pakhala
recipes.description: A cooling curd-based fermented rice from Odisha, whisked with yogurt and tempered, eaten through the hot summer months.

steps.instruction: Cook the rice until soft, drain and cool completely to room temperature.
Add cold water to the cooled rice and let it rest for a few hours or overnight for a mild ferment.
Whisk the curd smooth and stir it into the rice water along with salt, grated ginger and chopped green chili.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves, and pour the tempering over the dahi pakhala.
Garnish with coriander and serve chilled.

recipes.name: Ghee Anna
recipes.description: Fragrant Odia ghee rice cooked with whole spices and finished with generous ghee, a temple-style comfort meal.

steps.instruction: Heat ghee in a pot and fry the cashews until golden, then set them aside.
In the same ghee, add bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom and let them sizzle to release aroma.
Drain and add the soaked rice, stirring gently for a minute to coat every grain in ghee.
Pour in double the volume of hot water, add salt, and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the flame and cook until the water is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
Fluff with a fork, top with the fried cashews and rest covered for five minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Odia Mixed Vegetable Pulao
recipes.description: A lightly spiced Odia-style vegetable pulao with seasonal vegetables and whole spices, cooked in ghee.

steps.instruction: Heat ghee in a pot and sizzle bay leaf and cinnamon.
Add sliced onion and saute until soft and translucent.
Add all the chopped vegetables and saute for a few minutes until glossy.
Stir in garam masala and the drained rice, coating everything gently.
Add hot water and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until done.
Rest covered for five minutes, then fluff and serve.

recipes.name: Suji Upma
recipes.description: A soft, savoury semolina upma tempered with mustard, dal and vegetables, a common Odia breakfast.

steps.instruction: Dry roast the rava in a kadai until it smells nutty and turns pale golden, then set aside.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds and urad dal, then add curry leaves and green chili.
Add chopped onion and vegetables and saute until the onion softens.
Pour in about two and a half times water with salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the flame and add the roasted rava in a steady stream while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook until the upma thickens and pulls away from the pan, then serve hot.

recipes.name: Chuda with Onion
recipes.description: Beaten rice tossed with onion, green chili, coconut and mustard tempering, a quick dry Odia breakfast or tiffin.

steps.instruction: Rinse the poha in a colander and let it drain and soften while you prepare the tempering.
Heat oil, fry the peanuts until crisp, then splutter mustard seeds and add curry leaves.
Add chopped onion and green chili and saute until the onion turns soft.
Stir in turmeric and salt, then fold in the drained poha gently.
Add grated coconut, toss to combine, and serve warm.

recipes.name: Dahi Chuda
recipes.description: Beaten rice soaked in sweetened curd with banana and jaggery, a no-cook Odia breakfast eaten cold.

steps.instruction: Rinse the poha briefly and drain so it stays soft but not mushy.
Whisk the curd smooth with grated jaggery and a pinch of salt until the jaggery dissolves.
Fold the drained poha into the sweet curd and let it soak for ten minutes.
Top with sliced banana and a dusting of cardamom, and serve chilled.

recipes.name: Ghuguni
recipes.description: A hearty Odia yellow-pea curry simmered with potato and mild spices, a classic street tiffin often paired with bara.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked peas with the cubed potato, turmeric and salt until tender.
Heat oil in a kadai and crackle cumin seeds, then add chopped onion and saute till golden.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomato, chili powder and cook to a soft masala.
Tip in the cooked peas with their liquid, add garam masala, and simmer to thicken.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with bara or chuda.

recipes.name: Odia Aloo Dum
recipes.description: Baby potatoes simmered in a light onion-tomato gravy with panch phoron, a popular Odia breakfast side with puri or chuda.

steps.instruction: Halve the boiled potatoes and lightly fry them in a little oil until the edges crisp, then remove.
In the same oil, crackle panch phoron, then add chopped onion and saute until golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and fry, then pour in the tomato puree with turmeric, chili and cumin powder.
Cook the masala until oil separates at the edges.
Return the potatoes, add a cup of water and salt, and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Finish with coriander and serve warm.

recipes.name: Bara
recipes.description: Crisp, fluffy urad dal fritters fried golden, an iconic Odia tiffin usually served with ghuguni.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked urad dal to a thick, fluffy batter using minimal water.
Beat the batter well to incorporate air, then mix in chopped chili, ginger, onion, cumin, pepper and salt.
Heat oil in a kadai until a drop of batter rises quickly to the surface.
Wet your fingers, shape small rounds with a hole in the centre, and slide them into the oil.
Fry, turning once, until golden and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper and serve hot with ghuguni.

recipes.name: Dahi Bara
recipes.description: Soft urad dal fritters soaked in spiced whisked curd, a beloved Odia dahi bara aloo dum street snack.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked urad dal to a fluffy batter, add chopped chili and salt, and beat well.
Deep fry small rounds of batter until golden, then drain.
Drop the hot fritters into a bowl of warm salted water to soak and soften.
Whisk the curd smooth with a little water, roasted cumin, chili powder and rock salt.
Gently squeeze the water from each fritter and immerse it in the spiced curd for at least 30 minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve chilled, optionally topped with aloo dum.

recipes.name: Chakuli Pitha
recipes.description: A soft, mildly fermented Odia rice-and-dal pancake, thicker than dosa, eaten for breakfast with ghuguni or dalma.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked rice, urad dal and poha together with a little water to a smooth, slightly thick batter.
Add salt and let the batter ferment overnight in a warm place until it rises and turns airy.
Heat a tawa and grease lightly, then pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thick round.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges, cover, and cook until the base is golden and the top is set.
Flip and cook the other side briefly, then serve hot.

recipes.name: Arisa Pitha
recipes.description: A deep-fried Odia rice-flour and jaggery cake with a crisp exterior and chewy centre, made during festivals.

steps.instruction: Melt the jaggery with a splash of water to a thick syrup and strain out any impurities.
Mix the hot syrup gradually into the rice flour with cardamom to form a soft, pliable dough, then rest it.
Divide the dough, pat each portion into a small disc, and press sesame seeds onto the surface.
Heat oil in a kadai to a moderate temperature.
Slide in the discs and fry on low, spooning oil over, until deep golden and set.
Drain well and cool before serving so the centre firms up.

recipes.name: Manda Pitha
recipes.description: Steamed Odia rice-flour dumplings stuffed with sweet coconut and jaggery, offered during Manabasa Gurubar and festivals.

steps.instruction: Cook the grated coconut with jaggery until it thickens into a sticky filling, then add cardamom and pepper and cool.
Boil water with a pinch of salt, then mix in the rice flour off the heat to make a soft dough.
Knead the warm dough smooth and divide into balls.
Flatten each ball, place a spoon of coconut filling in the centre, and seal into a smooth stuffed dumpling.
Arrange the dumplings in a steamer and steam until they turn glossy and firm.
Cool slightly and serve warm.

recipes.name: Enduri Pitha
recipes.description: Fermented rice-and-dal batter with sweet coconut filling steamed inside fragrant turmeric leaves, an Odia Prathamastami delicacy.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked rice and urad dal to a thick batter, add salt, and ferment overnight until airy.
Cook grated coconut with jaggery until sticky, then flavour with cardamom and pepper and cool.
Take a fresh turmeric leaf or banana leaf, spread a layer of fermented batter over it.
Place the coconut filling along one half and fold the leaf over to enclose it.
Steam the folded parcels until the batter is cooked through and firm.
Unwrap and serve warm to enjoy the aroma of the leaf.

recipes.name: Chhena Poda
recipes.description: Odisha's iconic baked cheesecake of fresh chhena and sugar caramelised until the crust turns deep brown and smoky.

steps.instruction: Knead the fresh crumbled chhena with the heel of your palm until completely smooth and free of grains.
Mix in sugar, rava, cardamom, chopped cashews and raisins until evenly combined.
Grease a baking tin with ghee, optionally lining the base with sugar for a caramel crust.
Pour in the mixture, level the top, and bake in a preheated oven until the top is deep brown.
Cool completely so the cake sets, then slice and serve.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani
recipes.description: Slow-simmered black urad dal and kidney beans enriched with butter and cream, a Punjabi restaurant classic.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked urad dal and rajma, add fresh water and salt, and pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until the beans are completely soft and mashable.
Melt butter in a kadai, add ginger garlic paste and chopped onion, and saute until the onion turns soft and golden.
Add the tomato puree, red chili powder and salt, and cook until the masala thickens and oil separates at the edges.
Pour in the cooked dal along with its water and mash lightly against the side of the pan to release starch.
Simmer gently on low flame, stirring often, so the dal reduces and turns creamy and dark.
Stir in the cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, simmer two more minutes and serve hot.

recipes.name: Rajma Masala
recipes.description: Red kidney beans simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy, a beloved Punjabi comfort curry eaten with rice.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked rajma, add fresh water and a little salt, and pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until the beans are soft.
Heat oil in a kadai, crackle the cumin seeds, then add chopped onion and ginger garlic paste and saute until golden.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder and salt, and cook until oil separates from the masala.
Add the cooked rajma with its water and mash a spoonful of beans to thicken the gravy.
Simmer on low flame until the gravy thickens and coats the beans.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves, stir and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
recipes.description: Chickpeas cooked in a tangy, robustly spiced gravy, the quintessential Punjabi chole.

steps.instruction: Drain the soaked chickpeas, add fresh water and salt, and pressure cook for 6-7 whistles until soft.
Heat oil in a kadai and saute the chopped onion with ginger garlic paste until deep golden.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili powder and chana masala, and cook until the masala darkens and oil separates.
Add the cooked chickpeas with some cooking liquid and amchur, then mash a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Simmer on low flame until the gravy thickens and clings to the chickpeas.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with bhatura or rice.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi
recipes.description: A dry Punjabi stir-fry of potatoes and cauliflower tossed with cumin, turmeric and warm spices.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a kadai, crackle the cumin seeds, then add ginger and sliced onion and saute until soft.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder and salt, and cook until the tomato breaks down.
Add the potato cubes and cauliflower florets and toss to coat well in the masala.
Cover and cook on low flame, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Uncover, raise the flame briefly to dry out moisture and lightly brown the edges.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves, toss and serve hot with roti.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer
recipes.description: Soft paneer cubes in a smooth, spiced spinach gravy finished with a touch of cream.

steps.instruction: Blanch the spinach in hot water for two minutes, refresh in cold water, then blend to a smooth puree.
Melt butter in a kadai, crackle the cumin seeds, then add ginger garlic paste, green chili and chopped onion and saute until golden.
Add tomato puree and salt and cook until the masala thickens and oil separates.
Add the spinach puree and simmer gently, stirring, so the raw smell disappears.
Fold in the paneer cubes and garam masala and simmer just until the paneer is heated through.
Swirl in the cream and serve hot with naan or roti.

recipes.name: Paneer Butter Masala
recipes.description: Paneer simmered in a rich, mildly sweet tomato-cashew gravy finished with butter and cream.

steps.instruction: Boil the chopped onion, tomato and soaked cashews with a little water until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth puree.
Melt butter in a kadai, add ginger garlic paste and saute until the raw smell fades.
Add the strained puree and kashmiri chili powder and cook, stirring, until the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
Season with salt and sugar, add a splash of water for a smooth consistency and simmer.
Add the paneer cubes, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi and simmer gently.
Swirl in the cream and serve hot with naan or jeera rice.

recipes.name: Jeera Rice
recipes.description: Fragrant basmati rice tempered with cumin and whole spices in ghee, a simple Punjabi accompaniment.

steps.instruction: Heat ghee in a deep pot and crackle the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon and cloves until aromatic.
Drain the soaked rice, add it to the pot and gently toast the grains in the tempered ghee.
Pour in one and a half cups of water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the flame, cover and cook undisturbed until the water is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
Rest covered off the heat for five minutes, then fluff with a fork and garnish with coriander leaves.

recipes.name: Kadhi Pakora
recipes.description: Tangy yogurt and gram flour curry with soft besan fritters, a homely Punjabi favourite.

steps.instruction: Make a thick pakora batter with half the besan, chopped onion, a pinch of salt and water, then deep fry spoonfuls in hot oil until golden. Keep aside.
Whisk the sour curd with the remaining besan, turmeric, red chili powder, salt and three cups of water until lump free.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a deep pot, crackle fenugreek seeds, cumin seeds and dried red chili, then add ginger garlic paste.
Pour in the yogurt mixture, stirring constantly, and bring to a boil to prevent curdling.
Lower the flame and simmer, stirring often, until the kadhi thickens and the raw besan smell disappears.
Slide in the fried pakoras, simmer five minutes so they soak up the gravy and serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Aloo Paratha
recipes.description: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato, griddled with ghee, a classic Punjabi breakfast.

steps.instruction: Knead the wheat flour with salt and water into a soft pliable dough and rest it for fifteen minutes.
Mix the mashed potato with onion, green chili, coriander leaves, amchur, red chili powder, carom seeds and salt into a smooth filling.
Take a ball of dough, flatten it, place a portion of filling in the centre and seal the edges over it.
Dust with flour and gently roll out into an even round paratha without letting the filling break through.
Cook on a hot tawa, flipping once, until brown spots appear on both sides.
Smear ghee on both sides and roast until crisp and golden, then serve hot with curd and pickle.

recipes.name: Aloo Posto
recipes.description: Diced potatoes cooked in a fragrant poppy seed paste, a signature everyday Bengali dish.

steps.instruction: Grind the soaked poppy seeds with one green chili and a little water into a smooth thick paste.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai until it smokes lightly, then temper the nigella seeds and remaining green chili.
Add the potato cubes with turmeric and salt and saute until the edges turn translucent.
Add the poppy seed paste and stir to coat the potatoes evenly.
Add a little water, cover and cook on low flame until the potatoes are tender.
Uncover and cook off excess moisture until the posto clings to the potatoes, then serve with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Cholar Dal
recipes.description: Bengal gram lentils simmered with coconut, raisins and warm spices, a lightly sweet festive Bengali dal.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked chana dal with turmeric and salt until soft but still holding shape, around 3-4 whistles.
Heat ghee in a kadai and lightly fry the coconut chips until golden, then set aside.
In the same ghee crackle cumin seeds, bay leaf and dried red chili, then add grated ginger.
Add the cooked dal, fried coconut, raisins and sugar and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer on low flame, stirring, until the dal thickens to a pourable consistency.
Finish with garam masala, stir and serve hot with luchi or rice.

recipes.name: Begun Bhaja
recipes.description: Thick brinjal slices marinated in turmeric and chili, shallow fried in mustard oil until crisp.

steps.instruction: Rub the brinjal slices with turmeric, red chili powder, salt and rice flour and let them marinate.
Heat mustard oil in a frying pan until it smokes lightly, then reduce to medium.
Lay the brinjal slices in a single layer and shallow fry until the underside is deep golden.
Flip and fry the other side until both sides are crisp and cooked through.
Drain on paper and serve hot as a starter with rice and dal.

recipes.name: Macher Jhol
recipes.description: A light Bengali fish curry with potatoes in a turmeric and nigella spiced broth.

steps.instruction: Rub the fish steaks with a little turmeric and salt and shallow fry in hot mustard oil until light golden, then remove.
In the same oil temper the nigella seeds and slit green chili until fragrant.
Add the potato wedges and ginger paste and saute for a few minutes.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder and salt and cook until the masala coats the potatoes.
Pour in two cups of water, bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are almost done.
Slide in the fried fish, simmer gently for five minutes, garnish with coriander leaves and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Chingri Malai Curry
recipes.description: Prawns simmered in a fragrant coconut milk gravy with warm spices, a festive Bengali delicacy.

steps.instruction: Marinate the prawns with turmeric and salt, then lightly fry in hot mustard oil for a minute and remove.
In the same oil temper the bay leaf, cardamom and cinnamon until fragrant.
Add the onion paste and ginger garlic paste and saute until the raw smell fades and the paste turns light golden.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, sugar and salt and cook briefly to bloom the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer and cook so the gravy thickens slightly.
Return the prawns and simmer just until cooked through and tender, then serve with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Luchi
recipes.description: Soft, puffy deep-fried flatbreads made from refined flour, a Bengali festive breakfast staple.

steps.instruction: Knead the maida with salt, sugar, ghee and water into a smooth firm dough and rest it covered.
Divide into small balls and roll each into an even small disc, oiling the board lightly instead of dusting with flour.
Heat oil in a kadai until hot, testing with a small piece of dough that should rise immediately.
Slide in a luchi and gently press it under the oil with a slotted spoon so it puffs up.
Flip once and fry until pale and puffed, keeping it white rather than browned.
Drain on paper and serve hot with cholar dal or aloo dum.

recipes.name: Bengali Aloo Dum
recipes.description: Baby potatoes slow-cooked in a spiced tomato and ginger gravy, a classic Bengali dum aloo.

steps.instruction: Heat mustard oil in a kadai and fry the parboiled baby potatoes with a pinch of turmeric until golden all over, then remove.
In the same oil temper the cumin seeds and bay leaf, then add the ginger paste.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder, sugar and salt and cook until oil separates.
Return the fried potatoes and toss to coat well in the masala.
Add a little water, cover and cook on low flame so the potatoes absorb the flavours.
Sprinkle garam masala, cook off excess gravy and serve hot with luchi.

recipes.name: Chanar Dalna
recipes.description: Fried paneer cubes simmered in a light gingery tomato gravy, a popular Bengali vegetarian curry.

steps.instruction: Fry the paneer cubes in hot oil until light golden and the potato cubes until they colour, then set both aside.
In the same oil temper the cumin seeds, bay leaf and cardamom, then add ginger paste.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, cumin powder, sugar and salt and cook until oil separates.
Add the fried potatoes with a cup of water, cover and cook until the potatoes are almost tender.
Add the fried paneer and simmer a few minutes so it softens and soaks up the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and serve hot with luchi or rice.

recipes.name: Mishti Doi
recipes.description: Sweetened caramelised yogurt set in earthen pots, the iconic Bengali dessert.

steps.instruction: Boil the milk in a saucepan and simmer, stirring, until it reduces to about two thirds of its volume.
In a separate pan caramelise half the sugar to a deep amber, then carefully stir it into the reduced milk.
Add the remaining sugar and cardamom, stir to dissolve and let the milk cool until just warm.
Whisk the starter curd until smooth and gently mix it into the lukewarm milk.
Pour into earthen pots or bowls and set undisturbed in a warm place until firmly set.
Chill in the refrigerator for a few hours before serving.

recipes.name: Khaman Dhokla
recipes.description: Soft, spongy steamed gram-flour cakes tempered with mustard seeds and finished with a sweet-tangy drizzle.

steps.instruction: Whisk besan, rava, curd, turmeric, salt and a little water into a smooth lump-free batter of thick pouring consistency. Beat well to incorporate air.
Mix in the green chili-ginger paste. Grease the steamer plate and bring water in the steamer to a rolling boil.
Add Eno to the batter, sprinkle a few drops of water over it, and gently fold as it froths. Immediately pour into the greased plate.
Steam covered until a toothpick inserted comes out clean and the top springs back.
Cool slightly, then cut into squares.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add slit green chili and curry leaves. Add a splash of water with sugar and a pinch of salt, boil briefly.
Pour the tempering evenly over the dhokla so it soaks in. Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney.

recipes.name: Methi Thepla
recipes.description: Thin, soft spiced flatbreads made with wheat flour and fresh fenugreek leaves, a classic Gujarati travel food.
