steps.instruction: Combine wheat flour, besan, chopped fenugreek, turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, ginger-garlic paste, sesame seeds, salt and 1 teaspoon oil in a bowl.
Add whisked curd and knead into a smooth, medium-soft dough using a little water only if needed. Rest 10 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll each thinly on a floured board into a round thepla.
Cook on a hot tawa, flipping once, and smear a little oil on both sides until golden-brown spots appear.
Press gently with a spatula so it puffs, then repeat with remaining dough. Serve with curd or mango pickle.

recipes.name: Gujarati Kadhi
recipes.description: A silky, lightly sweet yogurt and gram-flour curry tempered with cumin, cloves and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Whisk curd, besan, grated jaggery and salt with about 250 ml water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour into a pot, add grated ginger and slit green chili, and bring to a boil while stirring continuously so it does not curdle.
Lower the flame and simmer, stirring often, until slightly thickened and frothy.
In a small pan heat ghee and crackle mustard seeds, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Pour the tempering into the kadhi, stir, garnish with coriander and serve hot with steamed rice or khichdi.

recipes.name: Khandvi
recipes.description: Delicate rolled ribbons of cooked gram-flour and buttermilk batter, tempered with mustard and sesame.

steps.instruction: Whisk besan, curd, turmeric, ginger-chili paste, asafoetida and salt with about 150 ml water into a smooth thin lump-free batter.
Pour into a heavy pan and cook on low-medium heat, stirring continuously to avoid lumps, until it thickens to a spreadable paste.
Working quickly while hot, spread a very thin layer of batter on the back of greased plates or a clean countertop.
Let set for 2-3 minutes, cut into strips and roll each strip tightly into neat rolls. Arrange on a plate.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, sesame seeds and curry leaves, then spoon the tempering over the rolls.
Garnish with grated coconut and coriander and serve.

recipes.name: Avial
recipes.description: A medley of mixed vegetables simmered in a coconut-cumin paste and curd, finished with raw coconut oil and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Cook drumstick, raw banana, carrot, beans and ash gourd with turmeric, salt and a little water until just tender but not mushy.
Coarsely grind grated coconut with cumin seeds and green chili using minimal water.
Add the coconut paste to the cooked vegetables and simmer gently, tossing so vegetables coat evenly.
Lower the heat, stir in whisked sour curd and warm through without boiling so it does not split.
Turn off the flame, drizzle raw coconut oil, scatter curry leaves, cover for a minute and serve.

recipes.name: Olan
recipes.description: A mild, soothing ash-gourd and cowpea stew simmered in thin and thick coconut milk with green chilies.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked cowpea until soft but holding shape; drain and set aside.
In a pot cook the ash gourd and pumpkin with slit green chilies, salt and just enough water until tender.
Add the cooked cowpea and thin coconut milk (dilute half the coconut milk with water) and simmer briefly.
Pour in the thick coconut milk, warm gently without boiling, and adjust salt.
Turn off the flame, add curry leaves and drizzle raw coconut oil. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Cabbage Thoran
recipes.description: Shredded cabbage stir-fried with coconut, green chili and a mustard-urad dal tempering, Kerala style.

steps.instruction: Lightly crush grated coconut with green chili, a little turmeric and shallots to a coarse mix.
Heat coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, add urad dal, broken red chili and curry leaves and fry until dal turns golden.
Add shredded cabbage with remaining turmeric and salt, toss well.
Cover and cook on low, stirring occasionally, until cabbage wilts and is just tender but still bright.
Add the coconut mixture, toss on high for a minute until dry and fragrant, then serve.

recipes.name: Kadala Curry
recipes.description: Black chickpeas simmered in a dark roasted-coconut and spice gravy, the classic Kerala partner to puttu.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook the soaked black chickpeas with salt and turmeric until soft; reserve the cooking water.
Dry roast grated coconut with shallots on low heat until deep golden-brown, then grind with the spice powders and a little water into a smooth dark paste.
Heat coconut oil, saute onion and ginger-garlic paste until soft, then add the roasted coconut paste and cook until oil separates.
Add the cooked chickpeas with reserved water, stir in garam masala and simmer until the gravy thickens.
In a little oil crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves, pour over the curry and serve with puttu or appam.

recipes.name: Kerala Fish Curry
recipes.description: Tangy fish simmered in a fiery Kashmiri-chili and coconut gravy soured with kokum, cooked in coconut oil.

steps.instruction: Make a paste of chili powder, coriander powder and turmeric with a splash of water.
Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard and fenugreek seeds, then saute shallots, ginger, garlic and curry leaves until soft.
Add the spice paste and fry on low until the raw smell goes and oil separates.
Add soaked kokum with its water and enough water to make a thin gravy, add salt and bring to a boil.
Slide in the fish pieces, cover and simmer gently, swirling the pan rather than stirring, until the fish is cooked.
Stir in coconut milk if using, warm through without boiling, and rest before serving so flavors deepen.

recipes.name: Gongura Pachadi
recipes.description: A tangy Andhra chutney of sauteed sorrel leaves ground with roasted spices and finished with a garlicky tempering.

steps.instruction: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek and dried red chilies until aromatic, then set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil and saute the gongura leaves until they wilt, darken and the moisture evaporates.
Grind the roasted spices coarsely, then add the sauteed gongura and salt and grind to a thick chutney without water.
Heat remaining oil, crackle mustard seeds, urad dal, crushed garlic and asafoetida until garlic is golden.
Stir the tempering into the chutney. Serve with hot rice and a drizzle of oil.

recipes.name: Pesarattu
recipes.description: A protein-rich Andhra crepe of ground whole green gram batter, crisped on a griddle and topped with ginger and onion.

steps.instruction: Grind soaked green gram with rice, green chilies, half the ginger, cumin and salt into a smooth pourable batter using minimal water.
Heat the griddle, sprinkle a few drops of water and wipe, then keep it moderately hot.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread outward in a spiral into a thin round crepe.
Sprinkle chopped onion and remaining ginger over the top, drizzle oil around the edges and press lightly.
Cook until the base is crisp and golden, fold over and serve hot with ginger chutney or upma.

recipes.name: Gutti Vankaya
recipes.description: Small brinjals stuffed with a roasted peanut, sesame and coconut masala, then simmered in a tangy tamarind gravy.

ingredients.prep: small, slit into quarters keeping stem

steps.instruction: Grind roasted peanuts, sesame, dry coconut, coriander seeds, chili powder, turmeric and salt into a coarse dry stuffing masala.
Slit each brinjal into quarters keeping the stem intact and stuff generously with the masala; reserve leftover masala.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves, then gently place the stuffed brinjals and shallow-fry, turning, until skins blister.
Remove brinjals, saute onion and ginger-garlic paste in the same oil, then add reserved masala and cook until fragrant.
Add tamarind extract and water to make a gravy, return the brinjals, cover and simmer until soft and oil floats on top.
Rest a few minutes and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Tomato Pappu
recipes.description: Comforting Andhra toor dal cooked with tangy tomatoes, green chilies and a garlicky ghee tempering.

steps.instruction: Pressure cook toor dal with tomato, onion, green chili, turmeric and a little water until soft and mashable.
Mash the cooked dal well, add chili powder and salt with enough water to reach a pouring consistency and simmer.
Heat ghee, crackle mustard and cumin seeds, add broken red chili, crushed garlic, curry leaves and asafoetida until garlic browns.
Pour the tempering into the dal and stir.
Simmer for another minute and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Andhra Chicken Curry
recipes.description: A fiery Andhra-style chicken curry with a roasted spice base, ginger-garlic and plenty of red chili.

steps.instruction: Marinate chicken with half the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, half the chili powder, curd and salt for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, add cloves and cinnamon, then saute onions with curry leaves until deep golden.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste and cook off the raw smell, then add tomatoes and cook until pulpy.
Add remaining chili powder and coriander powder, fry on low until oil separates from the masala.
Add the marinated chicken and saute on high to seal, then lower heat, add a little water, cover and cook until tender.
Sprinkle garam masala, simmer until the gravy is thick and coating, and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Kanda Poha
recipes.description: Fluffy flattened rice tossed with onions, turmeric and a mustard tempering, finished with lemon and coriander.

steps.instruction: Rinse the poha in a colander until soft, drain well and let it sit; sprinkle salt and sugar over it.
Heat oil, fry peanuts until crisp and remove, then crackle mustard and cumin seeds with curry leaves and green chili.
Add potato cubes and cook covered until tender, then add onions and saute until soft and translucent.
Add turmeric, stir, then gently fold in the drained poha and fried peanuts until evenly coated and heated through.
Turn off the heat, squeeze in lemon juice, garnish with coriander and serve hot.

recipes.name: Sabudana Khichdi
recipes.description: A fasting favourite of soaked tapioca pearls tossed with crushed peanuts, potato and green chili in ghee.

steps.instruction: Gently mix drained sabudana with crushed peanuts, rock salt and sugar so the pearls stay separate.
Heat ghee, add cumin seeds, curry leaves and green chili, then add potato cubes.
Cover and cook the potatoes on low until soft and lightly golden.
Add the sabudana-peanut mix and toss gently on low until the pearls turn translucent and soft; do not overcook or they clump.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and coriander, toss and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Pithla
recipes.description: A quick, rustic Maharashtrian gram-flour curry with onion, garlic and green chili, best with bhakri.

steps.instruction: Whisk besan with about 200 ml water into a smooth thin lump-free slurry and set aside.
Heat oil, crackle mustard and cumin seeds, add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chili and crushed garlic.
Add onion and saute until soft, then add turmeric and salt.
Lower the flame and pour in the besan slurry while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook, stirring, until it thickens and the raw besan smell disappears; add water to reach desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with bhakri or rice.

recipes.name: Batata Bhaji
recipes.description: A simple turmeric-yellow Maharashtrian potato stir-fry with mustard, green chili and curry leaves.

steps.instruction: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, cumin and urad dal, then add asafoetida, curry leaves and slit green chilies.
Add sliced onion and saute until soft and translucent.
Add turmeric and salt, stir, then add the boiled cubed potatoes and toss to coat evenly in the yellow tempering.
Sprinkle a little water, cover and cook on low so the flavors meld and potatoes soften further.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and coriander and serve with puri or as a filling for vada.
